newsitem.title: USA: Builders report drop in US housing market index.
newsitem.headline: Builders report drop in US housing market index.

text.p: The National Association of Home Builders on Thursday reported a drop in its Housing Market Index, which it said reflects concern over a gradually slowing market and possible increases in interest rates.
The index, which measures the housing market on a scale of zero through 100, with zero the worst and 100 the best, fell to 54 in May from 56 in April, the association said.
"Clearly, builders are concerned about conditions in the market," said Kent Collins, executive vice president of the association.

The index is based on the group's monthly survey of its members in which it asks builders to rate present sales of single-family detached homes, sales expectations over the next six months and the traffic of prospective buyers. A rating of 50 would mean that roughly equal numbers of respondents reported good and poor conditions.
In May, the second consecutive month in which the index declined, each of the index's three components decreased.

The Commerce Department has reported that sales of new single-family homes fell 2.5 percent in March and construction starts of homes fell 6.4 percent in March. It will report April housing starts Friday at 0830 EDT (1230 GMT).
